newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Kabila's Congo bans use of Russian pilots, planes.
newsitem.headline: Kabila's Congo bans use of Russian pilots, planes.

text.p: President Laurent Kabila's government has banned the use by local airlines of Russian pilots and old Soviet-made planes in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Transport Minister Henri Mova told state television.
Mova, in comments broadcast on Sunday, said that stringent measures needed to be taken to improve the battered image of the former Zaire's civil aviation.

In the worst of a string of accidents across the then Zaire, a Soviet-made Antonov transport plane flown by two Russians crashed on takeoff onto a Kinshasa market in 1995, killing at least 330 people. An inquiry blamed overloading and human error.
"I'm not anti-Soviet, but I have noticed that those who hired Russian pilots did not respect the international legislation," Mova said.

"They don't speak French, they don't speak English. They have manuals written in the Russian language which we don't understand. We don't know their qualifications and the condition of their aircrafts," he said.

The television said Mova announced the ban during the talks with representatives of local air companies in Kinshasa on Saturday, adding that Congolese airlines that did not abide by the laws would be barred as well.

The new Congo, formerly Zaire, has about 100 private air companies. In the former Zaire many companies bribed officials. Their planes, popularly known as flying coffins, flew to dubious destinations, often smuggling diamonds or other contraband.
The Russian pilots of the Antonov that crashed on the market were jailed for two years but freed as Kabila's forces entered Kinshasa in May after ousting dictator Mobutu Sese Seko.
